goal: Decide whether another local repair is justified after repeated relation-semantic failures.
procedure: Separate preservation from capability. Confirm the frozen parent remained intact, verify heldout stayed closed, inspect whether dev errors are random or structured, then classify the failure as architectural when repeated local repairs preserve old capability but fail to recover the missing semantic distinction.
constraints: do not open heldout without dev readiness
do not authorize another local hotfix from a structured architecture-level failure
decision_criteria: role accuracy collapsed to a systematic global endpoint preference
authority: May classify the failure and close further gradient work; may not promote, scale, or change frozen gates.
validation: Magnolia execution completed 0:0; parent tensors unchanged; heldout not evaluated.
failure_or_lesson: Repeated local repair should stop when the failure geometry stays structured after preservation is solved. At that point, inspect the information path and task decomposition instead of tuning another router.
notes: Reusable seed: distinguish 'repair failed because old skill was forgotten' from 'repair failed because required information is absent or inaccessible upstream.'

goal: Locate whether directional relation semantics are preserved in the graph's raw pooled query, the trained semantic projection, or token-level contextual states.
procedure: Using one frozen checkpoint and fresh audit-only queries, compare role-gloss discrimination, opposite-role pair distance, and per-relation accuracy across raw mean pooling, the trained semantic projection, and parameter-free token late interaction. Perform no gradient or model mutation.
authority: Diagnostic only. Does not authorize training or architecture mutation.
failure_or_lesson: A downstream subsystem can appear incapable when the interface feeding it compresses away useful distinctions. Before adding downstream capacity, compare alternate frozen representations from the same upstream model.
notes: Token-level states retained substantially more directional signal, but causes/supports remained at chance; therefore the correct conclusion was mixed rather than 'token interface solved it.'

goal: Determine whether missing directional relation semantics exist at earlier frozen transformer layers and are weakened by later representation shaping.
procedure: Evaluate every hidden-state output of the frozen semantic backbone with the same relation-role audit. At each layer measure token late-interaction accuracy, mean-pool accuracy, opposite-role pair distance, and relation-specific causes/supports accuracy. Do not train.
constraints: no automatic architecture change from the measurement alone
decision_criteria: whether causes/supports rise above chance in any layer
whether final-layer degradation indicates information loss across depth
authority: Diagnostic only. May inform where a future interface taps the frozen semantic model; does not authorize training by itself.
failure_or_lesson: Relational capability can be layer-local. A final representation may hide distinctions present at intermediate layers. Future formation systems should preserve access to intermediate token features and diagnose layer locality before declaring an upstream capability absent.
notes: Especially valuable FBM seed: layer 12 recovered causes/supports to 0.625 while the final layer returned both to 0.5, showing that final-layer-only interfaces can misdiagnose available capability.
